accepts.because: one conversational turn to be remembered verbatim -- ONE message carries ONE turn and its own provenance, so identity travels per message and two turns of one session may name two different people (GH #272); a closed session batch is no longer a shape this lane takes. `session_id` and `turn_id` travel as ingress context, `happened_at` on the hop for historical ingest. The provenance of the turn travels the same way and is NOT optional: `audience_set` (a JSON list of participants in affinity vocabulary, `*` alone meaning universal) and `channel` are required, and `speaker` for a user turn or `agent_id` for an assistant turn names who spoke -- absent, the stored `speaker` stays empty, never the role. Without an audience or a channel the turn is refused on `reject` -- who was present is the gate on every later read, it cannot be inferred afterwards, and a guessed audience is worse than a missing turn. The conditional pair `speaker`/`agent_id` is deliberately NOT in the `context` list above: that list names keys a caller must have promoted, and it cannot say `exactly one of these two`. So the list carries the four keys that are always required, and the fifth requirement lives here in prose -- visible rather than implied, and not something the declaration will ever check for you

a question against this memory. The five recall keys (recall_query, memory_tier, recall_as_of, recall_window_from, recall_window_to) come as context, always all five, empty string = unset. The asking round comes with them and is required: `audience_now` (a JSON list of who is present right now) and `channel` (where the question is being asked); `channel_open_history` is optional and defaults to '0', '1' saying this room shows joiners its history. Without `audience_now` or `channel` the question is refused on `reject` rather than answered unfiltered -- a recall without an audience is not a recall with an empty one. TWO MORE KEYS are read and neither is in the list above, for the same reason `channel_open_history` is not: the list names what a caller MUST have promoted, and a key with a default is not one of them. `session_id` scopes the session read -- the tier-0 leg reads the episodes of THAT session, and a question that names none reads a session called 'default', which in a live colony is nobody's. `recall_caller` is a REPLY-TO TOKEN this hive never reads: whatever a caller puts there rides through untouched and comes back on `hop.recall_caller` of the `bundle` and of a `reject`, which is how ONE hive serves SEVERAL askers and each of them gets ITS answer (GH #532). The token has to change compartment on the way out, and this hive is the only place that can do it for every caller at once: left on the hop it would not survive, because the `recall` cell forms its own hop and only context travels (GH #411), and a door guarded on context ALONE is condemned by crates/meclaw-cells/tests/gh173_shipped_hive_contracts.rs AND ONE KEY IS READ TWICE (GH #536): `audience_now` is the audience gate's yardstick and, since the self leg, ALSO an IDENTITY -- its `member:`/`person:` tokens are the people this question is asked by, and a question in the first person ("what are my sons called?") anchors on them because it names nobody else. That is a second reading of a key the caller already promotes, not a new requirement: nothing has to be wired for it, and it widens no disclosure -- an anchor decides what is LOOKED UP, never what is seen, and every row it nominates is still measured against the same gate. GH #936: `hop.affect_filter` (optional, a JSON object as text: valence_max, valence_min, arousal_min, min_confidence) keeps only candidates whose source episode carries an affect mark inside it -- applied after the audience gate, never widening it; a malformed one is refused on `reject` with `invalid_input`. Every candidate of the record carries `affect` (null = unknown). GH #948: a body that carries `subject` (a canonical subject, 1..200 characters, matched in the store's normal form) and optionally `limit` (1..20, default 10) is a SUBJECT question instead: the newest facts of that subject, not expired, not replaced, as one `bundle` whose JSON names the `subject` -- under the same set rule as every read here (the round a subset of a fact's round, `*` universal, a fact without participants readable by nobody). Its asker promotes none of the recall keys and no `channel` (the question is not asked in a room, so the open-history clause never applies); `audience_now` is required, and a round declared empty (`[]`, an asker outside any conversation) reads only what was released to everybody. Without a declared round it is refused (`missing_audience`); a subject or limit out of form is `invalid_input`. `recall_caller` routes the answer home exactly as for any question.

a block the front model decided to remember NOW, in the inline contract form; it is bound to the newest user or peer turn of the caller session (refused as `ambiguous_speaker` when the turns it may answer name more than one speaker, GH #849; a fact that names its speaker as `source` is bound to that participant's turn instead, or dropped as `unknown_source` when no such turn is among them), so the session must be in the context. So must the provenance, on the same terms as `in_episode`: `audience_set` and `channel` are required and the block is refused on `reject` without them. The inline ingress writes facts directly, so it is the one lane where a missing audience would mint an untagged row without an episode ever refusing it first

a session that just ended, to be read WHOLE once (GH #300, ruling Q9). Per-turn annotation is blind in one direction -- the front model annotates the turn it has just answered and cannot know the turn after it -- so this lane is where a correction three turns later, a value the conversation only settled at the end and a claim the session itself retracted get sharpened. Nothing travels in the body: the lane names a session and the hive reads its own turns. The three keys are the same provenance every write lane of this hive demands, and for the same reason -- the pass proposes writes, so `session_id` says WHICH session is being closed, `audience_set` and `channel` say who was present and where, and a pass without them would mint sharpened rows nobody can filter afterwards. The shipped caller has all three already: `talky`'s `./session-keeper -> ./collector` close edge promotes exactly this set. What the pass did leaves on `close_report`; a pass that stopped leaves on `reject`

write this hive's remembered content OUT as a declared, versioned document (#243). `hop.export_to` names the run's directory, relative to the fence this hive's store declares in `params.transfer.base_path`; without it the hive's own name. The store writes `<dir>/memory-hive/seed/<table>.jsonl` for every table of the walk itself and `export_final.json` last, and the hive says `export_done` naming the directory (GH #555) -- a directory without the marker is not a document. Provenance travels with every row because the export projects every column of every table: a column nobody selects is a column that never leaves the store

take such a document into this RUNNING hive, idempotently. Since 3.3.0 it is ONE message and the WHOLE directory (GH #261): `hop.import_from` names the run directory the export wrote, nothing travels in the body and nothing is inferred. Every `seed/<table>.jsonl` of it is parsed before the first row is written, and every table of the call is applied in ONE transaction, so a document that is refused anywhere writes nothing at all -- not even the tables ahead of the refusal, and that holds for a broken file as well as for a table whose columns no longer agree with this store. Applying the same directory twice leaves the same state; that is what makes it a backup and a merge rather than only a birth seed. A document whose declared schema disagrees with this store by a single column, in either direction, is REFUSED on `reject` with nothing written: an imported row whose participant set did not survive is a row that may be told to anyone

GH #936: mark how one remembered turn read -- the body carries `affect: {episode_id | session_id + turn_id, valence (-1..1), arousal (0..1), confidence (0..1), source}` and `hop.affect_tag` (at most 64 characters) is echoed on the answer. The address `session_id` + `turn_id` names the INCOMING turn of that turn, never the agent's own answer. The asking round is `audience_now`, the reader's round as on `in_query`: the mark is written only on an episode that round may READ (the subset rule, `*` universal, an episode without an audience readable by nobody), so a round cannot learn that a turn it was not part of exists by being allowed to annotate it. The last write wins; the column holds the current reading, not a history. This hive recognizes nothing -- the reading comes from whoever sends it, and the mark is never a ranking signal of `in_query`.

GH #948: another part of the colony names the spellings a thing is talked about under and the id it carries there -- body `{aliases: [{alias, canonical}], force?}`, 1..32 entries, `alias` 1..200 characters, `canonical` an id `<prefix>-<rest>` of at most 64 characters from [a-z0-9_-]; `hop.alias_tag` (at most 64 characters) is echoed on the answer. Each spelling becomes a row of the subject alias table, keyed in the store's normal form, and ONE `canonicalize` of the subject column follows, so every fact said under that spelling -- before the binding and after it -- carries the id as its canonical subject; no fact is rewritten. A spelling that already means ANOTHER id is refused per entry with `alias_taken` unless `force` is true; the same id again is no conflict. Without `force` the write is an `insert` on the alias table's key and a `select` closes the same store bundle, so two requests in flight for one spelling never both bind. A request out of form writes nothing. No round: the alias table carries no audience -- a binding says what a spelling MEANS, never what anybody said -- and the answer never names a taken spelling's previous id, because a target may be a subject the nightly identity round derived from conversations, and no shape of that string tells it apart from an id. Answered by exactly one `alias_ack`.

one `memory_recall` call a brain decided to make, split out by a dispatcher and carried here by the member the asker stands in (GH #552). The body is the tool_call turn and nothing else -- `hop.tool_name` says which tool and `hop.tool_call_id` is the correlation the asking round is waiting on. The tier is NOT in it: how deep a recall runs is configuration of this hive (`./tool` params.tier), never a model argument, because a model that could choose its own depth could ask for one the instance was tuned away from. The round the question is asked in is required exactly as on `in_query` -- `audience_now` (a JSON list of who is present) and `channel` (where it is asked) -- and a recall without an audience is not a recall with an empty one: it is refused, and the refusal comes back as the call's own result

a collector asking this memory what its tool looks like, by NAME -- `{"tools": ["memory_recall"]}`, or `["*"]` for everything this hive declares, which is one schema. Whoever is reached declares themselves (GH #552): until this lane the schema was a hand-typed projection of THIS hive's `in_query` contract, kept in a collector one composite away and seeded a second time into a brain. It is not a tool round and carries no `tool_name`. The lane, the body and the answer are the tools hive's own, byte for byte, so a collector cuts this answer together with a tools hive's without knowing which of them was which

a model package for this hive's model call, pushed by the colony's llm-registry (GH #858): a PARAMS-ONLY body -- an empty `system` slot, no `messages` -- that the llm cell merges into its live params and answers with nothing. It goes from this path straight to the llm cell it is addressed to (`./closer`, `./dialectic`, `./dreamer`, `./judge`), past every other cell, because a params body is not a request. This hive has 4 llm cells, so the door reads `hop.subscriber` -- the cell path the registry addresses a push by -- and one edge per cell carries only the pushes whose path ends in that cell's name. The guard is permissive (the form of GH #478): a message with no subscriber at all -- which the registry never sends -- would reach every llm cell, and that is what lets the substrate's lane check see a door for the lane. The llm cell takes package keys from a params-only message only (GH #853), so no request on another lane can change the model it runs on. Draw it only from the registry's `update` lane, restamped `in_model`

emits.because: the answer to a question: the recalled material, fused and ranked, for whoever asked. WHICH of them asked is `hop.recall_caller`, carried back off `context.recall_caller` exactly as the asking round put it there and empty when it put nothing (GH #532). This hive serves one member and more than one asker inside it -- a conversation surface and a reasoning core today -- and the token is the only thing in the answer that tells them apart. It is handed back, never read and never interpreted

something this hive was sent and would not take -- a block it cannot bind, a half window it will not guess at, a turn or a question whose audience or channel is missing (`hop.reject_reason` is then 'missing_audience' or 'missing_channel'). Since 2.3.1 it also carries what this hive's OWN STORE would not do -- the transfer lane included, which since 3.3.0 names only `export_write_failed` and `import_failed` and puts the substrate's own transfer code (`transfer_seed_malformed`, `transfer_io_error`, `transfer_path_out_of_bounds`, `import_schema_drift`, ...) on `hop.store_error` beside it, for exactly the reason this sentence gives: a lane whose read or write came back refused stops there and says so, with `hop.reject_reason` = 'store_refused', `hop.store_error` carrying the store's own `error_code` and `hop.store_operation` naming the op that was refused (GH #343) -- including the nightly consolidation, which has no caller of its own and reports on this lane rather than nowhere. The code rides in `store_error` rather than inside `reject_reason` on purpose: the store's code list is OPEN (`invalid_input`, `query_timeout`, `write_denied`, `unknown_table`, `unknown_column`, `constraint_violation`, `sql_error`, ...), and a reason enum that had to grow with it would turn the next new code into a failed emit. The body says which and why. Drain it: undrained, nobody ever learns the memory was not written and the caller waits for a bundle that never comes. A refusal on the RECALL lane carries `hop.recall_caller` home exactly as a bundle does (GH #532): the asker that cannot be told its question failed is the one that waits longest

a model package pushed through `in_model` that one of the four llm cells refused (GH #863): its error, with that cell's own path in `hop.refused_subscriber` and the model the push named in `hop.refused_model`, leaves here instead of reaching the glue or `./recall` as a verdict -- before 3.6.1 the four cells' out-edges carried no condition, so a refusal was read as the cell's answer. A push addressed to another cell (one a forward brought here) is refused as `invalid_input` without the two keys and still reaches the verdict edge -- the forward that caused it is the defect. The builder draws one edge from here to the registry's container, which carries it back to the registry's `in_refused` lane; without one the refusal dead-letters `no_route`, loudly

what the close pass did with one closed session (GH #300, ruling Q9): how many turns it read, what it sharpened and what it left alone. It is the ONLY positive signal the lane has -- the pass writes through the inline ingress, which answers nobody, so without this the caller cannot tell a pass that ran and changed nothing from a pass that never ran at all. Drain it: undrained, the pass costs one strong-model call per session and reaches nobody, which is the same disease as an undrained export

this hive has written itself out completely: every table of the walk stands as `<seed_dir>/<table>.jsonl` and the completion marker `export_final.json` stands beside them, written last and by one rename, so a reader that watches the marker never meets a directory that is still filling. `hop.export_hive` names the hive, `hop.seed_dir` the directory RELATIVE to the fence the store declares (`params.transfer.base_path`), `hop.export_of` how many tables travelled and `hop.rows_written` how many rows. It is the lane that says an export is a BACKUP rather than a stack of messages, and it replaces the walk that used to say so in sixteen `dump` parts (GH #555)

the receipt of ONE applied import: `hop.export_of` counts the tables the document applied, `hop.rows_written` the rows that were NEW (so zero means the target already had every one of them), and `hop.export_final` is always '1' because since GH #261 a directory is applied whole or not at all and there is no part sequence left to be the last of. Since 0.30.0 the lane carries nothing else -- an export writes its own files and reports on `export_done` (GH #555), so the `dump_kind` key that told the two apart is gone with the distinction. Drain it with a PLAIN `hop.route == 'dump'` edge -- an edge that tests a second key reads as no drain under the required_drains probe. Undrained, it becomes `no_route` in the dead-letter queue, which is where the shipped member leaves it (GH #284 state 2): the receipt localises itself with its sender and its trace instead of being dropped inside a cell that read it and said nothing

GH #936: the one answer of `in_affect`. `hop.episode_id` and body `affect_ack: {episode_id}` name the episode -- the caller's own id on a refusal, the resolved one once written -- and `hop.error_code` says what happened: '' written, 'not_visible' unknown OR not readable by the round (one answer for both, so the lane is no existence oracle), 'missing_audience' no round, 'invalid_input' a key out of form or range (`hop.error_key` names it). Every answer carries the same keys and never the episode text. A store refusal leaves on `reject` instead. Drain it: undrained, a recognizer cannot tell a filed mark from a refused one.

GH #948: the one answer of `in_alias`. Body `done` (spellings bound by the request) and `refused` (`{alias, error_code}` per spelling not bound: `alias_taken`, the previous id never named, or `store_refused`); `hop.error_code` '' (judged and written), 'invalid_input' (nothing written, `hop.error_key` names the place, e.g. `aliases[2].canonical`) or 'store_refused' (`hop.error_key` names the op; a refused `canonicalize` leaves the spellings bound and the facts to the next one); `hop.alias_tag` echoed. Every answer carries the same keys. Drain it: undrained, a caller cannot tell a bound spelling from a refused one.

the answer to one `memory_recall` call, as one tool_result turn under the original `tool_call_id` (GH #552). A refusal answers HERE too -- a missing audience, a half-open window, a store that said no -- because a call that is not answered stalls the asking round until its idle window runs out; `hop.error_code` carries the recall cell's own `reject_reason` verbatim, and the caller reads it off the message exactly as it does for any other tool

this memory's OWN declaration, one `{name, description, parameters}` for `memory_recall`, plus in `unknown[]` the asked names it does not serve. Provider-neutral, like the tools hive's answer. A lane of its own and NOT `tool_result`: a result belongs to a call somebody made, this belongs to a start-up question. Since 3.4.0 it also carries `sidecar[]` ([#606](https://github.com/mmeyerlein/meclaw/issues/606)): the section this memory asks for IN RETURN, `{section: "memory", required: true, schema, instruction}`, on every answer of the lane including the one that served no asked name -- a section is not a response to a name, it is what this hive asks of whoever talks to it. An asking collector merges the offers of all its answerers and composes one block contract out of them (GH #529, one column over)

required_drains.because: since 2.1.0 a turn without a participant set or without a channel is REFUSED rather than written (#244) -- undrained, the refusal is silent and the caller believes a memory was kept that never existed, which is the one failure this gate exists to prevent
a block this hive refuses leaves on the reject lane -- undrained, nobody ever learns the memory was not written and the caller waits for a bundle that never comes
a question this hive will not answer -- a half window it will not guess at -- leaves on the reject lane; undrained, the asker waits for a bundle that will never arrive

the report is the pass's only positive signal -- it writes through the inline ingress, which answers nobody. Undrained, one strong-model call per closed session runs, costs money and reaches nobody, and nothing anywhere says whether it ever ran
a pass this hive stopped -- the store refused the session read above all -- leaves here; undrained, a close pass that did nothing looks exactly like one that sharpened everything it found
the export IS this lane -- wired without it, the store writes its seed set and nobody is ever told where, or that it finished at all
an export the store refused leaves here, and it is the only signal there is: no marker is written, so the directory is not a document and a reader that trusts a prefix trusts a lie
the receipt of an applied document is the only positive signal an import has -- undrained, nobody ever learns whether a transfer landed
a document this hive will not take -- one whose schema no longer agrees with this store above all -- leaves here with nothing written; undrained, a refused transfer looks exactly like one that landed

a caller that hands this hive a call and does not take the result back has stopped its own tool round half way: the recall runs, costs what it costs, and answers into nothing while the brain waits for a name it will never see again

a collector that asks this memory what it serves and does not subscribe to the answer offers its model a menu without `memory_recall` in it -- and the round then looks like a model that chose not to ask its memory, which is the one failure nobody can see from the outside
a mark a recognizer sends and whose answer nobody takes back is indistinguishable from a mark that was refused -- the lane writes into memory, and the only proof it did is this answer
a mark the store refused to read or write leaves here; undrained, the recognizer waits for an acknowledgement that never comes

a binding a caller sends and whose answer nobody takes back is indistinguishable from one that was refused as taken -- the lane moves which facts answer to an id, and the only proof of what it did is this answer

description.purpose: Scope marker of the memory hive: bundles the durable store and the write/recall/extraction/consolidation lanes of one MEMBER's memory behind ITS OWN PATH (ADR-0002 E1 -- agents are lenses on it, a second agent of the same member inherits what that member knows). `params.ports` is empty, so no edge reaches a cell in here; a caller names the hive and a lane on `hop.route`. The transfer lane (#243) carries the content OUT as a versioned document and back IN to a running hive, so a memory is an asset with an identity of its own rather than a side effect of one deployment. The recall tool (#552) is the same memory reached the way a model reaches any tool: `tool_call` in, one `tool_result` out, and the declaration handed out on `in_schemas` by the hive that enforces it. The consolidation lane carries two model roles: the dreamer writes the change narrative, the judge decides identity for the nightly canonicalisation round.
description.use_when: Instantiate once per member; wire the lanes at the hive path in the same mutation. Every write lane needs the provenance of the turn on its ingress context (audience_set, channel, and speaker/agent_id), every read lane the asking round (audience_now, channel).
description.not_in_scope: No agent logic, no conversation state, no routing for the parent scope — the hive only carries its internal graph.
description.contract_in: Ten lanes, all at the hive path. in_episode -- remember this turn. in_query -- answer this question. in_remember -- take this block now (inline). in_close_pass -- this session is over, read it whole once. in_export -- write the remembered content out as a document. in_import -- take one part of such a document in, idempotently. tool_call -- one `memory_recall` call a brain made, correlated by `hop.tool_call_id` (#552). in_schemas -- what does that tool look like. in_affect -- file how one remembered turn read (GH #936). in_alias -- these spellings mean this id (GH #948); `in_query` with a `subject` asks for the newest facts of one canonical subject. Which cell serves a lane is this hive's business.
description.contract_out: Seven lanes, out of the hive path. bundle -- the answer to a question. close_report -- what the close pass did with one session. dump -- the transfer document, part by part, and the receipt of an applied part. reject -- something this hive would not take; the body says which and why. tool_result -- the answer to one `memory_recall` call, refusals included, stamped `hop.tool_name = memory_recall` on the way out (GH #937 -- an observer of named tools filters on it). tool_schemas -- this memory's own declaration of that tool (#552). alias_ack -- what an `in_alias` bound and refused (GH #948).
